conventions.axes: Y-up, right-handed; camera looks down -Z by default; ground is the XZ plane at y = 0
conventions.lightIntensity: three.js physical units (directional/hemisphere/ambient: lux-like; spot/point: candela, decay 2)
conventions.easing: named functions from kit/time.js `ease` (formulas in references/kit-api.md)
conventions.camera: fov is vertical field of view in degrees (three.js convention); sensor-agnostic

style.name: Magnetic Memory
style.description: A bright white tabletop board holding a lattice of small two-tone latching tiles (matte cream one face, glossy indigo lacquer the other, vermilion edges), each on its own axle. A red-and-silver bar magnet on a dark handle sweeps a curve over the board: tiles under it swing over in a wave and stay flipped when it leaves. A weaker, higher pass with the magnet turned over flips only some back. Every tile's flip time is the first moment the pull at its cell beats its own seeded threshold along the magnet's known path, so any frame is computed directly. Neutral tone mapping, soft key light, hard tiles, no liquid.
motion: Every tile has its own flip times from memory.js: the first moment the magnet's pull at its cell beats its seeded threshold.
A flip is a closed-form damped swing about the tile's axle (about 0.3 s); before it, a pushed tile leans toward the magnet.
After the magnet leaves, nothing moves: the track is pure memory.
Camera: locked holds joined by short eased moves (no drift): top-down, three-quarter, a low raking glide along the track, high wide.

notes.title: It remembers
notes.mechanism: memory.js: 56 x 30 latching tiles, seeded initial states (33 % dark) and log-normal thresholds. The magnet is a two-pole vertical bar whose pose is a cubic-Hermite curve in t; a tile flips at the first time the push against its current face beats its threshold (found once at load by sampling the path every 1/240 s). Pass 1 red end down at 16 cm traces an arch; pass 2 turned over (silver end down) and 46 cm up runs straight across the board and cuts a narrower pale lane through both arms of the arch, flipping back only tiles whose threshold its weaker pull beats.
notes.sound: one click per 1/30 s bin of flips (gain ~ sqrt(count)), quiet ticks for the beat-1 settle, sparser lower clicks on pass 2; soft pad bed; whooshes as the magnet arrives and leaves.
